extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and news reporters learning feature and event reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reporting exhibitions, shows, parades, banquets, holiday celebrations and other special occasions, emphasizing selection of details that convey the mood, vivid descriptive treatment, and how to handle speeches and grouped interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of story (display vs special occasions)
rubrics_metrics.description: News stories in this division may be grouped in two classes : (1) those of display, such as exhibitions, shows, fairs, and parades, and (2) those of banquets, holiday celebrations, and other special occasions, such as college commencements. Although the subject matter covers a wide range, the method of handling the news is much the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which class the event fits (display or special occasion) to choose appropriate emphasis and treatment; despite varied subjects, apply the same basic methods of selection and descriptive treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose — portray events and bring out the spirit of the occasion
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in these stories is not only to portray attractively the events and scenes but to bring out the spirit of the occasion. There is generally a dominant note in all these events, and the effectiveness of the description can be greatly heightened by selecting those details that bring out this note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and present details from the point of view of their value in showing the mood of the occasion; this yields a story more interesting than a mere recording of incidents. Emphasize the 'dominant note' or central impression when choosing what to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy as truth of sentiment (avoid fictitious details and sentimentality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy in news stories of this kind, therefore, is not simply faithfulness to fact, but truth of sentiment. Untruthfulness lies in adding fictitious details in an effort to heighten the appeal, and in substituting sentimentality for true sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure factual accuracy and truthful portrayal of the event's sentiment; do not invent or embellish details to manufacture mood, and avoid replacing authentic feeling with mawkish or manufactured sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment — dynamic, picturesque, and vivid description
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief problem in writing these stories is to select picturesque and significant phases from the large mass of available material, and to reproduce the scenes and incidents with vividness. In general the description is of the so-called dynamic type, in that all of the details are selected with the purpose of bringing out one impression rather than of giving a complete picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose vivid, picturesque details that together create a single strong impression; prefer dynamic, selective description over exhaustive, neutral cataloging. Use description as an opportunity to create atmosphere and immediacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holiday and banquet reporting — match emotional tone to occasion
rubrics_metrics.description: In descriptions of holiday celebrations an emotional appeal is possible because every festival and holiday has its own particular sentiment. Christmas is distinctly the children's day and is characterized by generosity. Memorial day is marked by patriotic reverence for dead heroes. Fourth of July by patriotic jollification, and Thanksgiving day by the idea of feasting. For banquets and similar occasions in which the spirit of good fellowship is the dominant note the descriptive method in a lighter vein is particularly appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the conventional mood of the holiday or social occasion and emphasize details that embody that sentiment; use a lighter descriptive tone for convivial events like banquets, and a more reverent or festive tone as the occasion requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling speeches and toasts at events
rubrics_metrics.description: When speeches and toasts are delivered in connection with these events, they are treated like other speeches and are fitted into the story as incidents of the occasion, or, if they are of sufficient significance, they may be played up as the feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether a speech is incidental color (integrate briefly into the scene) or the central feature (lead with or develop the speech). Use excerpts and context to show how a speech contributes to the event's mood or news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting details from the point of view of mood/value
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection and presentation of details from the point of view of their value as showing the mood of the occasion results in a story of much greater interest than does the mere recording of the different incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When faced with a large mass of material, prioritize details that reveal atmosphere, character, and the event's dominant impression; discard peripheral facts that don't serve the chosen angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for presenting a group of interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Three different forms for a group of several interviews (as shown in telegraph stories): (1) a lead summarizing general reaction followed by brief attributed quotes headed by names/positions ('Here is what some of them say:' with short quotations), (2) a city/descriptive dateline followed by an extended quoted or paraphrased statement from a named official with contextual commentary, and (3) geographically distributed short statements with attributions illustrating varied local responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a presentation form that fits the material and wire-copy constraints: use compiled short quotes to show consensus or range of opinion; use an extended attribution when a single source's reasoning is newsworthy; use multiple localized attributions to show regional variation. Format each quote with clear attribution (name and position).
